headline: The Great 113-Grammer Heist: Culinary Catastrophe Grills Nation
deck: Burgers and bureaucrats face off as fast food takes center stage in a national security investigation.
article:
In a shocking twist, America finds itself embroiled in a culinary crisis as a highly organized gang of gourmet chefs, posing as health inspectors, has executed a brazen heist of 3,400 113-Grammers from fast food establishments nationwide. The FBI has launched 'Operation Double Quarter Pounder,' deploying agents to patrol burger joints and conduct undercover sting operations at drive-thrus.

Local chains, gripped by paranoia, are now required to install biometric scanners at every 113-Grammer counter, leaving patrons bewildered as they scan their thumbs to procure what was once an unregulated indulgence. “I just wanted a burger, not a hostage negotiation,” lamented Leo Spatula, a regular at the now heavily fortified Grilled Glory on Highway 27.

As evidence mounts, experts warn that this culinary caper could reshape America’s fast-food landscape indefinitely. “If we cannot secure our 113-Grammer supply, who’s to say what will be next? Taco Tuesday is already at risk,” declared Chief Culinary Analyst, Gladys Sauté, with a gravity befitting a national emergency.

The theft has prompted interdepartmental scrutiny, as local police forces coordinate with federal agencies in a burger crusade that has left many citizens questioning whether their next meal might come with ID verification. “It’s not just a burger; it’s the American dream.” Thus, the nation bites its nails, awaiting the reappearance of its most iconic meal while grappling with the grim reality that the pursuit of fast food is now a full-blown kitchen nightmare.
author: Patty Flippin', Senior Burger Correspondent

oped.title: The Real Culprit? Those Infernal Hats!
oped.author: Baron von Burgerstein, Chief Cheese Aficionado
oped.body: As we sink our collective teeth into the 113-Grammer Heist scandal, let’s not mince words—this is not just a culinary crisis but a hat conspiracy of epic proportions. Who can trust a nation of burger-eaters when their heads are adorned by such audacious millinery? Just look at them! Those oversized caps and floppy beanies blur our ability to distinguish a quarter-pounder from a concrete block. Clearly, the snatchers were led by a rogue band of hat enthusiasts trying to distract us from the real issue: flavorless ketchup! I propose a revolutionary solution: mandatory helmet regulations for all fast-food patrons. Imagine the safety! With our heads protected, we can focus on the pressing matter of restoring dignity to our drive-thrus. So let us rally behind the true victors—those unyielding hats—and against this bizarre burger debacle!

stories.headline: Pickles and Precaution: Local Dill Thief Apprehended
stories.deck: Authorities warn against the consequences of vegetable-based vandalism.
stories.article:
In a bizarre culinary caper, local authorities apprehended a pickle thief in West Piqua, Ohio, after a months-long investigation. The notorious 'Dill Bandit' was caught red-handed at the Super Gramma’s Deli, attempting to abscond with over 2.27 kilograms of signature fermented cucumbers. Investigators linked the thief to a string of recent brine-related burglaries across the county.

Detective Roy Kersh, known for his meticulous attention to pickling protocols, claimed the suspect had an intricate plan involving a high-speed getaway in a vintage delivery truck painted like a large jar of relish. Residents of West Piqua are reportedly relieved, as the pickle situation had soured lives and sandwiches alike.
